channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Pakistan Violence Casualties Surge 83% in Q3 2026, Report Finds
item.description: Pakistan experienced an 83% rise in violence-related casualties during the third quarter of 2026, with over 1,415 people killed and 558 injured. Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were the primary areas of conflict, accounting for 98% of total casualties. Civilian deaths increased by 36%, and security force casualties rose by over 79%.

item.title: Canadian Prime Minister to Discuss Trade and Cooperation with Turkish President
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is scheduled to visit Turkey this month to meet with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The leaders will discuss ongoing free-trade negotiations and potential cooperation in the energy and defense sectors. This visit marks the first dedicated bilateral trip to Turkey by a Canadian leader aiming to reduce economic dependence on the United States.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Three Defense Officials Amidst Ongoing Resignations
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking defense officials. Kanysh Abubakirov, First Deputy Minister of Defense and Chief of the General Staff, was removed from his post. Almaz Zhumakeev, Deputy Minister of Defense, and Kanat Niyazbekov, Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces, were also dismissed. These changes follow a tragic incident in the Caspian Sea that resulted in the deaths of 14 soldiers.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aligns Veterinary Legislation with WTO Rules
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved amendments to the Law on Veterinary Medicine, aligning national legislation with World Trade Organization rules. The law emphasizes animal disease prevention, prioritizing prophylaxis, and ensuring the safety of animal products. It also coordinates state, departmental, and private veterinary activities and introduces risk management.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Child Protection Laws Against Violence
item.description: Uzbekistan has passed a new law enhancing child protection by strengthening legal measures against all forms of violence. The amendments increase accountability and introduce stricter penalties, particularly for sexual violence against children under 14. This initiative aims to ensure children grow up in a safe environment where their rights are protected.

item.title: Sole Survivor of Caspian Sea Incident Completes Military Service
item.description: Akzhol Temerkhan, the sole surviving conscript from Mangystau region in a recent Caspian Sea military exercise incident, has completed his mandatory military service. 17 servicemen were swept away by worsening weather; 14 died, three were rescued. Two criminal cases were initiated.

item.title: Almaty Court Sentences Ecologist Olzhas Duisenov to 7.5 Years in Prison
item.description: An Almaty court has sentenced ecologist Olzhas Duisenov to 7.5 years in prison for embezzlement. Duisenov, who denied all charges, was found guilty of misappropriating property. He was initially accused of corporate raiding and embezzling World Bank grant funds. He was arrested in February last year and has been in custody since.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates 80 Billion Tenge for Livestock Purchase Under 2026-2030 Plan
item.description: Kazakhstan has allocated 80 billion tenge to purchase 60,000 head of livestock as part of the Comprehensive Livestock Development Plan for 2026-2030. The plan aims to improve genetic potential and productivity. Over 7,000 cattle have already been imported from abroad since early 2026.

item.title: Flydubai Pilot Fights for Life, Recounts Saving Passengers During Attack
item.description: An Indian Flydubai pilot, Smith Machchhar, recounted his struggle for survival and efforts to save passengers after being attacked on a flight to Tel Aviv. He managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to subdue the assailant. The plane was safely diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Uzbek Senator Proposes Chemical Castration for Child Sex Offenders
item.description: Uzbek Senator Rustam Kalanov has proposed chemical castration for individuals convicted of sexual crimes against children, citing its use in other countries. Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbayeva suggested observing the practical application of new legislation first.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates German President and Chancellor
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has extended congratulations to the President and Chancellor of Germany on the occasion of their national holiday. The message conveyed wishes for prosperity and success to the people of Germany.

item.title: Uruzgan Youth Succumb to "Tablet K" Drug Use Amidst Unemployment and Taliban Claims
item.description: Residents of Uruzgan province express concern over rising youth drug use, particularly "Tablet K," attributing it to unemployment, easy drug access, and hard labor. They criticize the Taliban's anti-drug efforts, stating drug use has increased despite the declared ban.

item.title: Five Wildberries Representatives Join Management of Uzbekistan's National Postal Operator
item.description: Shareholders of Uzbekistan's national postal operator, UzPost, have elected a new supervisory board with five members linked to Wildberries & Russ. Wildberries stated their aim is to modernize the postal service and improve efficiency, potentially boosting e-commerce in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates German Leaders on Unity Day
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent congratulatory telegrams to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Chancellor Friedrich Merz on German Unity Day. Tokayev acknowledged Germany's resilience and progress, expressing gratitude for a recent warm reception during his visit and highlighting new opportunities for partnership.

item.title: Tokayev Congratulates German Leaders on National Holiday, Cites Stronger Partnership
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent congratulatory telegrams to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Chancellor Friedrich Merz on German Unity Day. He thanked them for a warm reception during a recent visit to Berlin, stating that agreements reached will boost joint projects and strengthen bilateral partnership.

item.title: Ecologist Olzhas Duisev Sentenced to 7.5 Years in Prison
item.description: An Almaty court sentenced ecologist Olzhas Duisev to 7.5 years in prison for misappropriation of property. Duisev was accused of illegally seizing a company that developed technology for cleaning soil and water from oil waste. He was also accused of embezzling World Bank funds, forging documents, and drug possession, charges he denied. Another defendant, Walikhan Shakirov, also received a 7.5-year sentence.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Congratulates Germany on Unity Day
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent congratulatory telegrams to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Chancellor Friedrich Merz on German Unity Day. Tokayev highlighted the development of bilateral cooperation and thanked German leadership for their hospitality during his recent official visit. Agreements reached in Berlin are expected to strengthen the strategic partnership and joint projects.

item.title: Afghan and Russian Health Ministers Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Afghanistan's Public Health Minister Noor Jalal Jalali met with Russian Health Minister Mikhail Murashko to discuss expanding long-term health cooperation. Topics included medicines, vaccines, medical equipment, training, and technology transfer. Jalali outlined Afghanistan's health sector needs, seeking greater Russian support. Murashko expressed Russia's readiness to enhance technical cooperation and bolster Afghanistan's health sector.

item.title: Alberuni University Students Denied Living Allowance for Lack of Beard and Cap
item.description: Students at Alberuni University report being denied living allowances by Deputy for Student Affairs Mushtaq Haqyar if they lack a beard and cap. Haqyar allegedly insults students, particularly Persian speakers, and bases eligibility on appearance rather than university rules. Students claim Haqyar stated trimmed beards are unacceptable and that allowances are withheld until beards grow longer.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. The dismissals follow the tragic incident during military exercises in the Caspian Sea where 14 servicemen died.

item.title: Kazakh President Dismisses Several High-Ranking Defense Officials
item.description: By order of the Head of State, several officials from the Ministry of Defense have been dismissed. This includes the First Deputy Minister of Defense - Chief of the General Staff, a Deputy Minister of Defense, and the Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Dismisses Three Senior Military Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking military officials. The exact reasons for the dismissals were not immediately specified, but they follow recent events within the armed forces.

item.title: Kazakh President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. The specific reasons for the dismissals were not immediately disclosed by the presidential administration.

item.title: Cost of Paid Military Service This Year Stands at 58,500 Somoni
item.description: The cost of paid or alternative military service this year is 58,500 somoni, equivalent to 750 indexation units. To be included in the list of individuals eligible for paid service, applicants must contact military commissariats.

item.title: Further Dismissals Occur Within the Ministry of Defense
item.description: The wave of dismissals within the Ministry of Defense continues. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev removed Kanysh Abdukirov, First Deputy Minister of Defense and Chief of the General Staff, Almaz Jumakeyev, Deputy Minister of Defense, and Kanat Niyazbekov, Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Replaces Top Military Officials Amidst Investigation
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed the Chief of the General Staff, a Deputy Defense Minister, and the Commander of the Naval Forces. These changes follow the death of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. A criminal investigation into negligence is underway, and a commission is reviewing the Ministry of Defense's operations.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Dismisses Defense Ministry Officials After Fatal Incident
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed several officials from the Ministry of Defense following a fatal incident at sea. The dismissals include the first deputy minister and chief of the General Staff. The actions follow an incident where 17 servicemen were swept out to sea, resulting in 14 deaths. Two criminal cases have been initiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Addresses Citizens Recruited for Ukraine Conflict
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has issued a statement regarding citizens allegedly recruited under false pretenses to fight in Ukraine. The ministry is taking the situation seriously and has established a hotline for relatives seeking assistance. Protecting citizens abroad is a top priority.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. This follows a recent tragedy on the Caspian Sea where 14 servicemen died. The president has ordered a comprehensive military reform to enhance security and readiness.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Quds Force Commander Calls for Strengthening Regional Defense Belt
item.description: Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, urged strengthening a "belt of defense, independence and dignity" stretching from Afghanistan to Yemen. He made these remarks at a ceremony in Tehran, emphasizing the need for enhanced regional security cooperation.

item.title: UAE Prosecution Investigates Flydubai Pilot's Attack as Attempted Terrorist Act
item.description: The UAE Public Prosecution is investigating the incident involving a flydubai pilot attacking the captain as an attempted terrorist act. The co-pilot allegedly used an emergency axe to seize control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Investigations into motives and connections are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Global Adoption of AI Accord Based on 'Washington Model'
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev advocates for the global adoption of an AI accord, inspired by the 'Washington Model' signed by U.S. tech leaders. He proposed this at the AI Development Council, suggesting it could form the basis of a UN treaty and announced Kazakhstan's intention to present its vision at the G20 Summit.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Reports Meeting with Donald Trump, Provides No Details
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, daughter of Uzbekistan's president, announced a meeting with Donald Trump on social media, accompanied by a photo. She expressed pride in the conversation. Details regarding the date and location were not disclosed, and the White House has not commented.

item.title: Iran Executes Five Afghan Citizens in September, Human Rights Group Reports
item.description: The Hengaw Human Rights Organization reported that Iran executed five Afghan citizens in September. A total of 68 prisoners were executed across Iran last month, a decrease of 23.5% from August. The primary charges for the executed Afghan nationals were drug trafficking and murder. Afghan citizens constitute the largest group of foreign prisoners in Iran.

item.title: Afghanistan Faces High Casualties from Unexploded Ordnance, UN Reports
item.description: Afghanistan remains among countries with the highest casualties from unexploded ordnance (UXO), with 64 incidents and civilian casualties recorded this year. The UN spokesperson stated that UXO poses a serious threat, especially to children. Efforts to clear contaminated areas are hampered by funding shortages.

item.title: Over 900 Afghan Migrants Return to the Country Through Border Crossings
item.description: The Taliban announced that 971 Afghan migrants, including 219 families, returned to Afghanistan through various border crossings on Friday. Hamdullah Fitrat, a Taliban spokesperson, provided figures for returns via Torkham, Pul-e Abrishum, Spin Boldak, and Islam Qala. UN and aid groups expressed concern about the impact on Afghanistan's capacity.

item.title: UAE Prosecutor General: Flydubai Co-pilot Intended Terrorist Act
item.description: The UAE's Prosecutor General stated that investigations into a Flydubai incident revealed the co-pilot attempted a terrorist act. During the flight, the co-pilot attacked the captain with an emergency axe in the cockpit, attempting to seize control of the aircraft. The plane, with 182 passengers, was reportedly brought to the brink of crashing due to the co-pilot's actions.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Implementation of Four Strategic Development Programs
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Economic Development and Trade reviewed the progress of four strategic planning documents focusing on green economy, education, кадровая политика, and tourism. The meeting, held on October 1, 2026, involved representatives from relevant ministries and departments. Decisions were made to ensure timely implementation of planned activities.

item.title: Iran Urges Iraq to Lift Restrictions on its Airlines Amid US Sanctions
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry has called on Iraq to act independently of US sanctions and lift restrictions on air travel between the two countries. Iran stated that these restrictions harm passengers and contradict the strategic relationship based on good neighborliness. Iran considers US sanctions illegal and a violation of national sovereignty.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Lower Age of Criminal Responsibility for Group Hooliganism to 14
item.description: Uzbekistan will lower the age of criminal responsibility for hooliganism committed in an organized group from 16 to 14 years. The law also introduces responsibility for creating and financing criminal organizations, and toughens penalties for hooliganism and intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm. Criminal liability for illegal martial arts competitions is also introduced.
